events.description: Taliban offensive begins in earnest. Roggio's count of Taliban-controlled districts rises from about 73 to about 142 of 407 by 24 June, i.e. 69 districts gained, mostly in the north.
Gen. Mark Milley testified to the House Armed Services Committee, implying about 30 districts had changed hands and downplaying the offensive because no provincial capitals had fallen.
Date the episode was recorded; used as the snapshot for district counts.
Taliban entered Kunduz city and fighting began there.
After a base was overrun in Takhar, the Taliban executed the local NDS chief and the police chief. It was the only execution Roggio had seen during the offensive.
President Obama ordered the surge in Afghanistan, which lasted through 2010 into 2011.
Gen. Nicholson called population control the 'most telling' metric for success in Afghanistan.
US/Resolute Support discontinued the district control and population metrics as of 'limited decision-making value'. Gen. Austin Miller shifted the success measure to a political settlement.
Roggio formalized his district-control map after an Afghan press report cited an anonymous official saying the Taliban controlled eight districts.
Alexander Kutowski helped migrate the map to Tableau, enabling real-time updates.
NATO, Resolute Support and U.S. Forces Afghanistan said district-control data was of limited decision-making value.
A U.S. official testified before Congress on the number of districts the Taliban controls. The hosts doubt the analysis behind the figure.
A person at NATO headquarters contacted Roggio about his map of Taliban district control.
Many districts fell to the Taliban in the preceding weeks.

key_claims: The Taliban gained about 69 districts between 1 May and 24 June 2021, taking control of roughly 142 of 407 districts, with about two-thirds of the gains in northern Afghanistan.

Afghan security forces are often surrendering districts and bases through negotiations via intermediaries, and the Taliban are mostly not carrying out mass executions, though a local NDS chief was killed in Takhar.
The Taliban are holding off on provincial capitals until the full Western withdrawal but are already encircling and assaulting them.
Hosts say the US military consistently downplayed Taliban control and ties to al-Qaeda, and dropped the district and population metrics in October 2018 when they showed a steady Taliban advance.
Hosts say al-Qaeda remains deeply embedded in the Taliban, citing its integration of Tajik and Uzbek groups in the north and its presence in Helmand.
The Afghan government's 'national uprising' framing is an unintentional admission of Taliban strength, and the militias risk being a return of the warlords.
SIGAR/Resolute Support maps used five control categories and undercounted Taliban control, e.g. rating three Helmand districts Taliban-controlled when about six were, partly because of reporting lag.
Hosts say U.S. and Afghan officials dislike Roggio's district-control map because it gives a more honest picture of Taliban gains.
Hosts say NATO, Resolute Support and USFOR-A dismissed the district data in 2018, and NATO is now asking for it.
Roggio says the Taliban mostly control Helmand province, contrary to Afghan official claims.
Hosts say the Taliban have taken many districts in recent weeks and doubt the Afghan government can retake most of them.
Hosts argue the map should have served as an alarm that the war effort was failing.
